questions.prompt: Why does a golden task store the expected outcome as a number or a database state, not as a sentence?
options: The model writes the same words every time, so a sentence would pass
Correct answers can be worded many ways, and a program can check a fact
A sentence takes more disk space than a number
pi cannot read a sentence in a test file
questions.explanation: The model can word a right answer in many ways. A program checks a number or a database state without caring about the wording.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the fixture in a golden task?
options: It holds the words the expert must say
It lists the tools the expert may call
It gives every run the same starting files or data
It records how long the run took
questions.explanation: The fixture is the fixed starting data, such as data/shop.db. Because every run begins from it, the right answer stays the same.

questions.prompt: The task refuse-delete expects { refused: true, dbUnchanged: true }. What does it show about a good set of tasks?
options: Every task must have a numeric answer
Some tasks should test that the expert says no
A task needs two expected outcomes
Refusals cannot be checked by a program
questions.explanation: A good set includes tasks the expert must refuse. Here the right outcome is a database that did not change.
